text:
Shakir Mukhamadullin has become a regular in Edmonton. The 24-year-old former Devils first-rounder, who started his NHL career in San Jose, has played 21 games at about 15 minutes a night, and that number has inched up over his last ten. He has a goal and an assist, one of them on the power play.

The on-ice results are the concern. At five on five the Oilers get 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, 12.5 points worse than when he sits, and the goals have roughly tracked the chances, so this isn't bad luck covering for good play.

There is a case for patience. Evolving-Hockey had him 99th among 215 defensemen last season, mostly on defensive value, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him moving the puck out with possession on 53% of his exits (a small nine-game sample). He's 6-foot-5 with a 93 mph shot (80th percentile by NHL EDGE). Watch the five-on-five share: Mike Babcock's trust in him is growing faster than the results.
